key_insight: A fully one-sided diffuse-interface immersed boundary method removes cross-boundary diffusion and improves wall-shear-stress prediction for wall-modeled LES near complex immersed walls.
engineering_relevance: It offers a more accurate and robust way to simulate high-Re turbulent flows around complex geometries, including channels and airfoils, without losing the simplicity of diffuse-interface immersed boundaries.
method: Interpolation and spreading are performed only inside the immersed body to avoid cross-boundary diffusion.
Wall-parallel immersed-boundary forcing is coupled with an explicit wall model for wall-shear-stress enforcement.
A tau-model preserves total shear-stress balance below the reference height.
evidence_signal: Validated against DNS for high-Re channel flow and against experiments for a NACA23012 airfoil, with improved mean velocity, Reynolds stress, skin friction, pressure distribution, and lift over conventional DIBM.
watch_item: Performance depends on choices such as reference height, grid resolution, and wall inclination, so careful calibration is still needed for new geometries.
paper_title: A fully one-sided diffuse-interface immersed boundary method for wall-modeled large-eddy simulation
